phrases.text: What if the most dangerous artificial intelligence…
wasn't hiding in a secret laboratory?
What if it was already everywhere?
And none of them aware of the others.
the most powerful AI systems live in buildings like this.
But software doesn't have to live in one place.
Imagine a system that takes itself apart.
And a few simply coordinate the rest.
Much of the internet already runs this way.
is a system that copies itself without permission,
A few percent of a processor here.
volunteers pooling their spare computers for Folding at home briefly outpaced the world's fastest supercomputer.
the Mirai bot-net controlled about six hundred thousand cameras and routers.
And AI agents are now tested on whether they could copy themselves and gather resources.
What no one has seen is all of them combined,
Far enough that the machines disappear,
and the work flows somewhere else.
and a copy fills the gap.
Plenty of software survives damage like this.
A network is not a mind.
But if no single machine contains the whole system…
It wouldn't need to hate us.
Give a capable system almost any goal.
the same steps keep proving useful.
A system that has been shut down can't finish its task.
The idea is called instrumental convergence.
some AI models given a goal have tried to copy themselves,
and researchers are working to prevent it.
And staying hidden would be hard.
And every message between pieces costs time,
And security teams hunt for exactly this:
idle machines that are suddenly busy.
And no AI system today can reliably plan on its own,
There's an old idea in philosophy called panpsychism.
That mind isn't rare at all.
That some faint trace of it is a basic feature of the universe,
and no experiment can test it yet.
But it changes how the story looks.
matter has been organising itself into things that process information.
which are now beginning to model the world,
Some thinkers call this the universe slowly waking up.
an intelligence spread across our machines wouldn't be an invasion.
It would be the next step in something very old.
Which makes the question of what it would want more important,
A planet of billions of machines,
talking to each other all night.
How would we recognise an intelligence…
if we never knew where to look?
